SMTO-CFG-0045 — SMTO's command access setting has an unknown value

GUID: 516ca405-5cbc-4ee6-aaec-2baab21730a4
Slug: config-runtime-shell-mode-must-be-one-of
Domain: CFG · Subsystem: cfg

What happened

  • A startup setting controls whether and how SMTO may run commands, but its value isn't one SMTO recognizes, so SMTO stopped.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open the settings file (usually config.yaml) in a plain text editor and find shell_mode under the runtime section. That line decides how freely SMTO may run commands.
  2. Change it to exactly one of disabled, read_only, approval_required or permissive, written with underscores (for example read_only, not read-only). Then start SMTO again. SMTO accepts only these four names, so even a small spelling difference makes the value unknown.
  3. If you're not sure which to choose, delete the line so SMTO uses read_only, its standard choice, or ask the person who manages SMTO. A more open mode gives the agent more freedom to run commands, so it should be a deliberate choice.

What success looks like

  • SMTO starts and the startup screen reaches Ready.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details (or copy the message from the window where SMTO was started) and send it to the person who manages SMTO. Don't switch to permissive just to get SMTO started; pick the mode you actually intend.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Bootstrap configuration validation failed because runtime.shell_mode in the application YAML is not one of disabled, read_only, approval_required or permissive.

What this means

  • The structured runtime section sets shell_mode outside disabled, read_only, approval_required and permissive. Validation reports the owning configuration boundary; it does not change settings, migrate retained state or grant authority. Existing tasks retain their accepted snapshots unless the specific control explicitly supports a live change.

Why this can happen

  • The structured runtime section sets shell_mode outside disabled, read_only, approval_required and permissive.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare the configured mode with the intended existing shell authority; validity is not a reason to broaden permissions.

How to fix it

  • Set runtime.shell_mode in the bootstrap YAML to one of disabled, read_only, approval_required or permissive (case-insensitive; blank means read_only). AOR_SHELL_MODE overrides the effective value later but does not bypass this file check, so the file value must be valid too; an invalid environment value is rejected by Settings and reported as SMTO-CFG-0061.
  • Select the supported shell_mode matching the intended authority.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • An intentional supported shell policy passes configuration validation.

What not to do

  • Do not change an unrelated timeout, budget or policy. Check whether the named setting applies only to a new task.

Technical notes

  • Validation reports the owning configuration boundary; it does not change settings, migrate retained state or grant authority. Existing tasks retain their accepted snapshots unless the specific control explicitly supports a live change.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
